question: MO-01 Democratic Primary Winner
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the nomination for the Democratic Party to contest the MO-01 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The Democratic primary will take place on August 4, 2026.

If no nominee is announced by November 3, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democrat sources, including https://democrats.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
I can't confirm anything about the outcome. Several search results were dated after July 17 and reported on the primary itself, so I set them all aside and used none of them below. Before July 17, Wesley Bell, the incumbent, appears to have been the favorite over Cori Bush. He had more money and AIPAC's backing, and the markets leaned toward him. No independent poll was found, and the race was competitive.

## 1. Resolution source
- I did not fetch democrats.org. In practice the nominee is set by the official results of Missouri's August 4 primary, certified by the Secretary of State, so the party has nothing to announce before then.
- 2026-03-31: Candidate filing closed. St. Louis Public Radio describes the Democratic race for the 1st District as a Bell vs. Bush rerun of 2024. [STLPR](https://www.stlpr.org/government-politics-issues/2026-03-31/7-takeaways-from-the-end-of-candidate-filing-for-missouris-august-primary)
- Ballotpedia appears to list some minor Democratic candidates too, but I couldn't load the page to check the full field. Maria Chappelle-Nadal, who ran in 2024, is running for the St. Louis County Council instead. [STLPR](https://www.stlpr.org/government-politics-issues/2026-07-09/three-longtime-political-figures-seek-1st-district-seat-on-st-louis-county-council)

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-07-17 nothing has settled the question. The primary is on August 4. Bell is the sitting congressman and Bush is the former member trying to win the seat back.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-07-15: Bell's second-quarter FEC report shows about $1.3M raised and about $1.9M cash on hand. I couldn't find Bush's second-quarter numbers. [Quiver Quant](https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Fundraising+Update%3A+Representative+Wesley+Bell+just+disclosed+%241.3M+of+new+fundraising)
- 2026-07-14: Bush is campaigning against Bell's position on Israel. Missouri Independent reports she expects to be outraised again. [Missouri Independent](https://missouriindependent.com/2026/07/14/cori-bush-targets-wesley-bells-israel-stance-in-st-louis-congressional-rematch/)
- 2026-07-09: Axios calls the race AIPAC's next big target. Its super PAC, the United Democracy Project, is spending again to oppose Bush. I couldn't open the article, so this comes from the headline and summary. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/09/aipac-missouri-israel-cori-bush-bell-primary)
- Around the same time, outside groups had reserved about $1.365M in ads backing Bell or attacking Bush, according to AP via Ground News. I couldn't confirm the exact date. [Ground News](https://ground.news/article/wesley-bell-sees-surge-of-outside-spending-ahead-of-rematch-with-cori-bush)
- Through March 2026 (FEC): Bell had raised about $1.9M and had about $1.2M on hand. Bush had raised about $831K and had about $120K on hand. [St. Louis American](https://www.stlamerican.com/news/local-news/familiar-choice-different-visions/)
- 2026 (February 19-23 fieldwork, released around April): a poll for Bush's campaign by HIT Strategies of 401 likely primary voters had Bell 44%, Bush 40%, undecided 17%, margin of error ±5.4. In the same poll 52% viewed Bush favorably and 45% viewed Bell favorably. This is the only public poll I found. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/ex-squad-member-cori-bush-chances-of-defeating-wesley-bell-in-missouri-race-12260748), [Drop Site](https://x.com/DropSiteNews/status/2044157672514011561?lang=en)
- Background: the Justice Department investigation into Bush's campaign spending on security, which involves payments to her husband, dates from January 2024. I found no 2026 developments in it. [1011now](https://www.1011now.com/2024/01/31/rep-cori-bush-is-under-doj-investigation-misuse-funds/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2024-08-06: Bell beat Bush, then the incumbent, about 51.2% to 45.6%. Chappelle-Nadal got 2.6%. AIPAC-linked groups spent about $8.6-9M against Bush. [Primaries Substack](https://primaries.substack.com/p/86-primary-preview-part-ii), [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2024-election/rep-cori-bush-loses-democratic-primary-campaign-onslaught-israel-group-rcna165306)
- 2024 polls were mixed and mostly paid for by interested groups. A Mellman poll for DMFI PAC, a pro-Israel group, had Bell up 43-42 in June and 48-42 in late July. An earlier poll had him up 50-28. [DMFI](https://dmfipac.org/news-updates/press-release/exclusive-poll-wesley-bell-opens-up-6-point-lead-over-rep-cori-bush-in-mo-primary/), [KSDK](https://ksdk.com/article/news/local/business-journal/poll-wesley-bell-beating-cori-bush-maria-chappelle-nadal-st-louis-congressional-seat/63-0d33f189-6458-4619-a902-4a2c4a27ac3f)
- In general, House incumbents almost always win renomination, usually above 95% of the time. Former members trying to beat the person who unseated them succeed much less often. I didn't look up a precise figure for that.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Newsweek, in an undated article from before the primary: Kalshi had Bell 59%, Bush 40%. A month earlier Kalshi had Bush ahead, 53% to 45.1%. Polymarket had Bell at about 64%. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/ex-squad-member-cori-bush-chances-of-defeating-wesley-bell-in-missouri-race-12260748)
- Polymarket market page: [link](https://polymarket.com/event/mo-01-democratic-primary-winner). I couldn't confirm its price as of July 17. Prices I saw from later dates are excluded.
- I found no Manifold market or expert race ratings for the primary.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late July: likely debates or joint appearances, more outside ad spending (UDP and progressive PACs), and pre-primary FEC reports covering through mid-July.
- Possible new internal polls from either side, and any developments in the Justice Department investigation.
- 2026-08-04: primary day, followed by certification of the results.
